strategy.summary: Reproduce PR #32351 (sklearn tree splitter, missing-value partitioning off-by-one) by building scikit-learn from source at buggy commit b1b01a1611e1, adding the developer's test_splitting_with_missing_values, and running it. On the buggy revision the test should fail at a random_state that tries the feature containing NaNs first (i=2 per the PR), where impurity comes out as [0.25 0.1875 0.1875] instead of [0.25 0. 0.]. On the fixed revision (the PR's change to the splitter) all 20 trees should match and the test should pass. The environment versions are not documented constraints; they are the issue #32178 reproducer's versions, adopted as a choice.

system_packages: gcc or clang with OpenMP support (libgomp on Linux)
OpenBLAS via the numpy/scipy wheels (no system BLAS needed)
build_commands: pip install numpy==2.3.3 scipy==1.16.2 Cython==3.1.3 joblib==1.5.2 threadpoolctl==3.6.0 meson-python meson ninja pytest
apply the reproducing test diff to sklearn/tree/tests/test_tree.py on the buggy checkout
after checking out the fixed PR commit, rebuild the editable install (the .pyx splitter changed) before running the test
pinned_because: No documented scikit-learn dependency constraint exists; the versions are the issue #32178 reproducer environment's, chosen by this plan rather than required by the evidence
numpy 2.3.3 and scipy 1.16.2 are numerically relevant and were observed with the bug, so they are pinned to match the reproducer
Cython, joblib and threadpoolctl are not numerically relevant and are pinned only for reproducibility
scikit-learn is built from source at the buggy commit (reported as 1.8.dev0); no version pin applies because the bug lives in the source being built

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy b1b01a1611e1 with the test diff applied: the test fails with an AssertionError from assert_array_equal on tree.tree_.impurity for some random_state in range(20) (i=2 per the PR), where the observed impurity is [0.25 0.1875 0.1875] against expected [0.25 0. 0.]. On the fixed PR commit (rebuilt): the same test passes, meaning all 20 fits give impurity [0.25 0. 0.] and no assertion fires.
strategy.numerical_probe: Loop i in range(20) (or 1000 with X[X==0]=np.nan) fitting DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=1, random_state=i) on the issue's X and y, and print tree.tree_.impurity and tree.tree_.n_leaves to see which random_state triggers the broken split. Counts are approximate and not used as a pass condition.

input_output_examples.input: X = np.vstack([[0,0,0,0,1,2,3,4],[1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2]]).swapaxes(0,1).astype(float); y=[0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1]; X[X==0]=np.nan; DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=1, random_state=i).fit(X, y) for i in range(20), reading tree.tree_.impurity
input_output_examples.buggy_output: [0.25 0.1875 0.1875] for the failing random_state (i=2 per PR #32351)

input_output_examples.input: same X with NaNs, y=[0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1], DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=1, min_impurity_decrease=0.25).fit(X, y) repeated 1000 times, reading tree.tree_.n_leaves
input_output_examples.buggy_output: n_leaves is 1 in roughly 500 of 1000 fits; np.bincount(n_leaves) approximately [0 500 500]
input_output_examples.expected_output: n_leaves == 2 for every fit; bincount approximately [0 0 1000]

risks: Platform: the evidence is from Linux x86_64 with OpenBLAS and libgomp. The bug is in splitter logic, not BLAS, so it should reproduce elsewhere, but this is unconfirmed on macOS arm64 or Windows; the test is only run on Linux here.

The failing random_state depends on sklearn's internal feature-order RNG. Changing the build's compiler or the RNG path could shift which i fails; the test loops over 20 seeds so it should still catch the bug, but this is not verified.
The buggy-to-fixed transition depends on checking out the correct parent commit b1b01a1611e1. If the local checkout differs, the bug may already be fixed or the splitter code may differ.
Editable builds are stale after checkout: the fixed revision must be rebuilt, otherwise the buggy compiled splitter still runs and the test will fail on both revisions.
The issue's min_impurity_decrease=0.25 differs from the test (default 0) and the PR snippet's 0.002; the test as written uses the default, so the reproducer should follow the test, not the issue.
The issue's bincount counts (~500 each) are approximate and should not be used as strict targets; only the test's assertion decides the transition.
No sanitizer or specific architecture is required by the evidence, so none is planned; if the bug turns out to need a different threading setting, that would be a new risk.

oracle.reference_source: the developer's assert_array_equal on tree.tree_.impurity against np.array([0.25, 0.0, 0.0]) in PR #32351
oracle.why: Impurity values here are exact binary fractions (0.25, 0.1875, 0.0), and the test compares with assert_array_equal, so the comparison is exact.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision, for the random_state that tries the NaN-containing feature first (i=2 per the PR), tree.tree_.impurity is [0.25 0.1875 0.1875] instead of [0.25 0. 0.]; assert_array_equal raises AssertionError, because the last non-missing sample was not partitioned correctly, so the impurity decrease is wrong.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision (rebuilt), the splitter partitions the missing-value case correctly, so tree.tree_.impurity is [0.25 0. 0.] for all 20 random_state values and the test passes with no assertion failure.
